**Worktree workspace model MEASURED: ticket-start --worktree works in v2, engram unifies across worktrees (git_remote), adopt for parallel team**

**What**: Decision to adopt `brain:ticket:start --worktree --base feature/v2.0.0` as the workspace model for the heterogeneous parallel team (Claude Code on D2, Antigravity on E1), replacing separate clones. Grounded in three measurements (owner asked to measure before proposing).

**Why**: The owner proposed worktrees-per-task (which brain 0.x supported) as the scale model vs n separate clones. Measured, it wins: cheap (shared object store, single fetch, zero-dep), natural one-branch-per-worktree lock.

**The 3 measurements**:
1. `ticket-start.mjs:138-207` STILL creates worktrees in v2 — the 0.x machinery was NOT retired. Wired as `brain:ticket:start`; `--worktree` does `git worktree add <parent>/<repo>-issue-<id> -b <branch> <base>`, supports `--base <branch>`, copies `.env` (not inherited by worktrees), runs feature-resume inside. So it's ADOPTED, not a revival micro-slice.
2. **engram does NOT fragment memory across worktrees.** Probed with a throwaway worktree: `git remote get-url origin` from the worktree = the identical origin URL as main (`https://github.com/csrinaldi/brain.git`). engram resolves project by `git_remote` (every mem_save this session reported `project_source: git_remote`), so a worktree = the SAME project "brain". The finding-#8 concern ("a worktree is another project by path") does NOT apply to git_remote resolution. The worktree's `.git` is `gitdir: <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>` — one shared object store, single fetch.
3. Antigravity's `trustedWorkspaces[]` auto-adds each new dir on trust, so each new worktree needs one operator "trust" action — a known minor operational step. Cleanup: strip scratch/worktree entries on teardown.

**Bonus**: `brain:ticket:start --worktree --base feature/v2.0.0` would have PREVENTED baptism finding #2 (Antigravity's PR was born pointing at `main` because the base was set manually) — the tool sets the base explicitly. Adopting worktrees removes an already-observed error class, not just adds scale.

**Where**: `brain/scripts/ticket-start.mjs`, `package.json` (`brain:ticket:start`). Base for all parallel work: `feature/v2.0.0`.

**Learned**: engram's project identity is the git remote, not the filesystem path — so any same-repo worktree/clone with the same origin shares one memory project. This is the mechanism that makes worktrees safe for the parallel team. Related: [[architecture/worktree-workspace-model]], [[reference/antigravity-cli-settings]], [[sdd/issue-256-b2/baptism-complete]].
